# Simulation, AI & Data Practice
::: {.lead}
Simulating strategic systems, learning agents, working with live data, and publishing the analysis as reproducible, documented R code.
:::
:::

## What you'll be able to do by the end

- Build Monte Carlo and agent-based simulations and run tournaments between strategies.
- Explain how AlphaZero, counterfactual regret minimisation and multi-agent reinforcement learning relate to game theory.
- Trace machine learning from the perceptron to transformers, with R implementations.
- Retrieve data from public sources such as the World Bank, ACLED, NOAA and arXiv for game-theoretic analysis.
- Produce publication-ready figures, interactive plots, game trees and network graphs.
- Make an analysis reproducible with Quarto, renv, targets and Docker, and package it with roxygen2, testthat and pkgdown.

## Who should take this course

For readers who already write R and want to simulate, learn from data, and publish their work reproducibly.

## The other courses

- [Course 1 — Foundations of Game Theory](../course1-game-theory/index.qmd) — Equilibrium concepts and the canonical games, decisions under uncertainty, evolutionary, cooperative, behavioural and network games, and the history behind them.
- [Course 2 — Mechanisms, Behaviour & Ethics](../course2-mechanisms-behaviour/index.qmd) — Designing the rules of the game, auctions, behaviour in the lab and the field, incentives in blockchains, ethics, and cases where theory meets reality.
- [Course 3 — Mathematical & Statistical Methods](../course3-methods/index.qmd) — Linear algebra, optimisation, information theory, statistics, Bayesian and causal inference, econometrics and network science: the toolkit behind the models.
